senses.gloss: f.(b. h.; ברך)blessing, bestowal of prosperity, good wishes, choice, plenty.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 5a:7">Keth. 5ᵃ</cite> <he>הואיל … ב׳ לדגים</he> because on it the blessing was given to the fish (<cite ref="Genesis 1:22">Gen. I, 22</cite>, to be fruitful). Y. ib. I, beg. 24ᵈ <he>אין כתיב ב׳ וכ׳</he> the blessing (<cite ref="Genesis 2:3">Gen. II, 3</cite>) refers not to man but to the day.—
<cite ref="Eruvin 63b:10">Erub. 63ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>תבא עליו ב׳</he> blessing rest upon him (he acts rightly).

<cite ref="Ketubot 103a:22">Keth. 103ᵃ</cite>; <cite ref="Bava Batra 144b:5">B. Bath. 144ᵇ</cite> <he>בִּרְכַת הבית ברובה</he> the blessing of a house consists in the number of inmates (every member of a household contributes to its comfort); <cite ref="Tosefta Ketubot 12:3">Tosef. Keth. XII, 3</cite> <he>ב׳ הבית מרובה</he>.

<cite ref="Bava Metzia 42a:5">B. Mets. 42ᵃ</cite> <he>אין הב׳ מצוייה וכ׳</he> blessing (unexpected supply, miraculous increase) will not take place in things which are weighed &c.; <cite ref="Taanit 8b:14">Taan. 8ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesachim 50b:10">Pes. 50ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אינו רואה סימן ב׳ לעולם</he> will never see a sign of prosperity; a. fr.

senses.gloss: benediction, prayer to be recited on certain occasions.
units: <cite ref="Berakhot 35a:20">Ber. 35ᵃ</cite> man must not taste anything <he>בלא ב׳</he> without a blessing.
<cite ref="Berakhot 40b:10">Ib. 40ᵇ</cite> <he>כל ב׳ שאין וכ׳</he> a benediction in which the Name of the Lord is not invoked, is no benediction; a. fr.
<cite ref="Shabbat 115b:2">Sabb. 115ᵇ</cite> <he>כותבי ב׳</he> those who write out the formulas of prayer.—

senses.gloss: B’rakhoth, the first treatise of the Mishnah, Talmud, a. Tosefta.—Compounds: בִּרְכַת אבלים the prayer for consolation inserted in the mourners’ grace after meal.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 8b:2">Keth. 8ᵇ</cite>; a. fr.—<he>ב׳ ארוסין</he> benediction preceding betrothal, v. <cite ref="A03043"><he>אֵרוּסִין</he></cite> <cite ref="Ketubot 7b">Ib. 7ᵇ</cite>.—<he>ב׳ הארץ</he> that portion of the grace after meal which refers to Palestine.
<cite ref="Ketubot 8b:2">Ib. 8ᵇ</cite>.—<he>ב׳ הזבח</he> the benediction before partaking of the festive offering (<cite ref="H00148"><he>חֲגִיגָה</he></cite>) which accompanies the Paschal lamb.
Pes. X, 9 (120ᵃ).—ב׳ הזימון the appeal to the partakers of a meal to say grace, common prayer.
<cite ref="Berakhot 45b:18">Ber. 45ᵇ</cite>.—<he>ב׳ חתנים</he> benediction on performing the marriage ceremony, also inserted in the grace after wedding meals during seven days.
<cite ref="Ketubot 8b:2">Keth. 8ᵇ</cite>.—<he>ב׳ כהנים</he> the priestly benediction (<cite ref="Numbers 6:24-26">Num. VI, 24—26</cite>).

<cite ref="Mishnah Sotah 7:6">Sot. VII, 6</cite>.—<he>ב׳ המזון</he> grace after meal. Keth. l. c.—<he>ב׳ המצוות</he> benediction on performing a divine command (of a symbolic nature). Ib. 7ᵇ.—<he>ב׳ רחבה</he> benediction of consolation pronounced in open air on the mourners’ return from burial (v. <cite ref="E00051"><he>הַבְרָאָה</he></cite>). Ib. 8ᵇ.—<he>ב׳ התורה</he> benediction before and after reading the Law.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 1:5:4">Y. Ber. I, 3ᶜ</cite>.—[For other compounds see the respective determinants.]
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 56a">Snh. 56ᵃ</cite> sq.; (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 8:4">Tosef. Ab. Zar. VIII</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 9:4">IX</cite>), 4 <he>קיללת</he>).
